headline: The journal Nature Synthesis has devoted an issue to self-driving laboratories, where robots and AI plan and run chemistry experiments, with a focus on industry use.
score_reason: Informative overview, but an editorial rather than a new finding.
importance_line: Chemists and drug companies weighing automated labs get an industry view of the barriers, including scale-up, standards and safety, but this is an overview and not a new result.
summary: A Nature Synthesis editorial introduces an issue on self-driving laboratories, which combine robotics, automation and AI to plan and run experiments, and on the difficulty of moving them from academic proof of concept to industrial practice. It points to RoboChem-Flex, a modular platform from Timothy Noël's group costing around US$5,000, and to a call for an "autonomy safety harness" to govern how AI-generated plans become real experiments.
